Subject: RE: Fwd: Final redlines for pilot SOW (liability/indemnity items) — legal assessment & recommended language

Karthik / team —

Reviewed Sapphire_Redlines_v3.pdf and SOW redline. Short assessment and recommended path below.

Assessment:
- Liability cap: Customer requests aggregate cap = 1x pilot fees (~$120k). Our standard cap (for pilots) is 6 months fees or $250k floor — this request lowers our upside and increases relative exposure.
- Indemnity carve-out: Their proposed carve substantially narrows our indemnity obligations for regulated-data claims. That is acceptable only if we also secure a limitation on their ability to bring indirect damages or consequential loss claims.
- Warranty: propose adding explicit acceptance testing criteria and a 30-day cure period for any alleged breach; this reduces ambiguous warranty exposure.

Recommendation (pilot-specific compromise):
1) Liability cap: set aggregate liability cap at the greater of $150,000 or the fees paid during the pilot. This splits the difference and keeps exposure bounded.
2) Indemnity: accept limitation to willful misconduct and gross negligence for regulated-data third-party claims, BUT carve back third-party IP claims to standard Redwood indemnity.
3) Warranty: include a defined acceptance test in SOW Exhibit A and a 30-day cure window; delete open-ended warranties.
4) Term & rollback: pilot exception expires with the pilot; for any follow-on enterprise agreement, revert to standard Redwood terms unless an explicit cross-functional approval is obtained.

This package reduces legal risk and is defensible operationally. However, any reduction of a liability cap below $150k or removal of indemnity for third-party IP requires an exec exception signed by CRO or CEO per our policy (see internal policy link).

If commercial is willing to absorb a concession (recommended: 12% onboarding discount + $15k implementation credit), I will prepare a short sign-off memo for Aditya with the exact language for his approval.

Laura Bennett
